 By Shaghil Bilali , ET Online Last Updated: Oct 22, 2026, 02:55:23 PM IST Follow us Share Font Size Abc Small Abc Medium Abc Large Save Print Comment Synopsis
 Dearness relief hike: The Bharat Pensioners' Samaj has formally addressed a letter to the cabinet secretary concerning the urgent need for a dearness relief hike for pensioners. They stress the importance of timely disclosures to support pensioners reliant on such adjustments. With expectations for a DR increase of 3% to 4%, many hope for this announcement before Dussehra, as any delay has caused disappointment among those looking to better manage their festive expenses. Listen to this article in summarized format
 Listen ET Online DR hike for pensioners is yet to be announced. Like central government employees who have long been waiting for the dearness allowance (DA) hike announcement, pensioners are also keen to know when their dearness relief (DR) hike will be announced.
Now, Bharat Pensioners' Samaj (BPS), an organisation that claims to have 10 lakh central government pensioners as its members, wrote a letter to the cabinet secretary today, requesting him to intervene and instruct concerned departments to announce the DR hike soon.
In a letter dated October 22, 2026, Avinash Rajput, secretary general, BPS, wrote to the cabinet secretary to intervene with the Department of Pension and Pensioners’ Welfare (DoPWW) and the Department of Expenditure (DoE), Ministry of Finance , for the early announcement and release of the pending instalment of the DR to pensioners and family pensioners. 
Also Read: DA hike: Why is there delay in DA hike announcement and when can government make it? 
 Pensioners were waiting DR hike announcement before Dussehra, BPS writes 
The BPS writes that the pensioners were expecting the DR hike announcement before Dussehra (October 21).
“The delay has caused disappointment and uncertainty among pensioners, particularly elderly and financially dependent pensioners who look forward to this additional amount to meet their household and medical expenses,” the letter reads.
The BPS says that the festive season brings additional household and family expenditure, making the timely release of the enhanced DR particularly meaningful.
“Dearness relief is not a bonus or a discretionary favour; it is an essential adjustment intended to mitigate the impact of rising prices on the fixed incomes of pensioners. Timely disbursement is, therefore, important for their financial security and peace of mind,” says the BPS.
Also Read: 8th Pay Commission gross salary hike: How Level 3 employees may get Rs 69,000 gross pay in 8th CPC 
The BPS requests the cabinet secretary to take up the matter with the DOPPW and the DOE for the early announcement and release of the pending instalment of DR, along with arrears, to pensioners and family pensioners.
“We sincerely hope that the government will consider this request sympathetically and take expeditious action in the larger interest of retired employees who have devoted their working lives to the service of the nation,” writes the BPS.
 DR applicable from July 2026 
The government calculates the DR on the basis of average 12-month retail inflation, measured through the All India Consumer Price Index – Industrial Workers (AICPI-IW). The new DR rate will be applicable from July 1, for which the retail average inflation of July 2025-June 2026 will be taken into account.
Once announced, pensioners will also get arrears for delayed months.
Also Read: 8th Pay Commission: Level 1 salary at Rs 47,160, Rs 54,000 or Rs 69,000? Check Level 1-5 estimates at different fitment factors 
 Can the DR hike be 3% or 4%? 
As per estimates, pensioners are likely to get a 3% DR hike, which can take the current rate of 60% DR to 63%. However, it will be known once the government announces it.
It was expected that the government would announce the DR rate after the cabinet meeting on Wednesday (October 21). However, the meeting didn’t take place, leaving lakhs of central government pensioners disappointed.
However, the government can announce the DR hike without a cabinet meeting also. But the long wait is testing the patience of pensioners. (Join our ETWealth WhatsApp channel for all the latest updates)
